text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In its 150-page submission to the Wallis inquiry into the financial system yesterday, the Reserve Bank launched a vicious attack on plans to create a single regulator for the entire financial system, claiming a "mega-regulator" supervising all financial istitutions could undermine the system's long-term stability. Page 1.

The Howard Government's hopes of establishing new players in the aviation market have crumbled with the failure of trans-Tasman newcomer Kiwi International Airlines, coupled with moves to fold another prospective operator, Pacific Transair. Kiwi Internatinal went into liquidation yesterday and the Australian Securities Commission has given notice that Pacific Transair faces a winding up application from a demountable building supplier. Page 1.

As building unions prepare to intensify industrial action in support of a claim for an increase of up to A$37 a week in travel allowances and the main building union warns it will push to increase site allowances on major new construction projects in Sydny, it is increasingly clear Australia's building industry faces major new cost pressures. Page 3.

After reporting a near doubling in net profit to A$36.5 million, Peter Harvie, managing director of Australia's largest radio network, Austereo Ltd , revealed he has spoken to the Government requesting that the law restricting it to two
stations in a single market be relaxed. He argued that a collection of licenses will ensure it more stable profits. Page 18.

Cinema and hotel giant Amalgamated Holdings Ltd, which owns the Greater Union cinema chain, Rydges hotels and resorts and Kosciusko Thredbo, has announced a three-for-one bonus share issue, injecting new liquidity into its shares after two years of outstading price rises. Amalgamated shares have skyrocketed from A$7 two years ago to as high as A$29.50 yesterday. Page 18.

Following a dramatic increase in the volume of electricity generated from its innovative power projects around Australia, independent power producer Energy Developments Ltd, which produces electricity from landfill gas, coal-seam gas and natural gas, has lmost doubled pre-tax profits. Page 18.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Twenty-three-year-old Steve Outtrim, who has seen phenomenal international success with an Internet software program he developed while out of work last year, will float 20 per cent of his company Sausage Software, founded last year, on the Australian Stok Exchange next month in an effort to raise about A$4 million. Page 1.

In a move which puts Westpac Banking Corp Ltd at odds with the major life companies and insurers, Westpac has urged the Wallis inquiry into the financial system to dump the existing rules for financial institutions, lock insurers and
non-banks out of the anking system and create a new consumer regulator. Page 19.

In its first year of new management under chairman Kerry Stokes and chief executive Gary Rice, the Seven Network Ltd has lifted profit by 32 per cent to a record A$116.5 million after tax and before abnormal items. However, because network programming costs appeared to remain high, Seven shares fell six cents to close at A$3.75. Page 19.

Investor confidence for listed entertainment stocks was boosted yesterday by the release of positive 1995-96 profit results from sector leaders Amalgamated Holdings Ltd, the operator of the Greater Union cinema chain and Rydges hotel and resort business, nd Austereo Ltd, who recently merged its 2DAY radio network and the five national Triple M stations. Page 19.

After recently reporting a jump in net profits to A$88.6 million for the six months to June 30, oil and gas major Santos Ltd announced yesterday it would stake a major claim for the petroleum assets of WMC Ltd, which are estimated to be
worth A$400 millio. Page 21.

Newcrest Mining Ltd managing director John Quinn, in New South Wales specifically for the announcement, confirmed yesterday his company will proceed with the A$440 million Cadia Hill copper-gold project near Orange in New South Wales, following State Govenment approval yesterday. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As submissions to the Wallis inquiry into the financial system closed yesterday, AMP called for approval for mergers between Australia's major banks and insurance groups, while Westpac Banking Corp said a life office should not be permitted to own a bank. AMP said concerns about the emergence of a single dominant financial institution because of the abolition of restrictions on mergers were unfounded. Page 25.

Strong earnings growth of 38 per cent based on increased advertising revenue in the capital cities to 33.5 per cent has helped lift Seven Network's annual net profit to A$115.1 million, compared to A$41.3 million last year. However, investors cut Seven'sshare price back six cents to A$3.75. Page 25.

Australis Media regional franchisee Austar has made a deal with Optus Communications to buy a new satellite service, which will see it able to provide 10 more channels of programming throughout regional Australia without relying on the
other major players Australis, Optus Vision and Foxtel. Page 25. --

Austereo, the owner of the 2Day FM and Triple M networks, yesterday announced a 97 per cent lift in annual net profit to A$36.5 million for the June 30 year, from A$19.8 million previously. Austereo increased advertising revenue by 25 per cent to A$139 mllion, despite the impact of the weak economy on the advertising market. Page 27.

The Smith's Snackfood Co has axed 60 staff, including one of Australia's most prominent marketing executives, Lisa Miles, in an effort to retain its share of the A$850 million snackfood category and "build a more customer and consumer focused business". Pge 27.

National Mutual Holdings managing director Geoff Tomlinson said yesterday that the group was well placed to pick up an operating licence in China in the not-too-distant future after being approached by the Chinese Central Bank to put in an application fora licence a year ago. Page 27.
THE AGE

The Seven Network yesterday announced a strong turnaround in earnings and an on-going commitment to news and current affairs, posting a rise in net profit to A$155.13 million in the 53 weeks to June 30, compared with A$41.26 million in the previous year. anaging director Gary Rice said while the company would continue to seek growth opportunities, the group's major focus was the strengthening of its television network. Page A1.

National Mutual Holdings managing director Geoff Tomlinson said yesterday that the company had a "reasonable chance" of being the first international group to secure a licence in China. Tomlinson told a Securities Institute of Australia lunch that while national Mutual was also looking at Thailand, India, Vietnam and the Philippines, the Chinese Central Bank last year approached National Mutual to put in an application for a licence. Page C1.

In its first formal submission to the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, the Reserve Bank yesterday slammed the idea of Australia being reduced to just two big banks, putting a dent in National Australia Bank's campaign to have the rules preventing bank mergers scrapped. Page C1.

Santos Ltd's A$88.6 million profit for the June-half largely reflects a change in the way realised/unrealised foreign-exchange gains are handled, with Santos ceasing to book foreign-exchange swings as abnormal gains or losses. Despite the flat profit, Satos is now considered a growth stock among
the listed oil and gas producers. Page C2.

Unable to carry forward tax losses, diverse entertainment group Amalgamated Holdings yesterday reported a 6.5 per cent fall in net profit to A$38.04 million for the year to 30 June. Chairman Alan Rydge said the result was in line with expectations and anounced a bonus issue of three new shares for every existing share. Page C2.

BTR plc yesterday conceded that it would book a loss of A$149.8 million against the sale of its Taiwan-based polymer manufacturing subsidiaries. The Taiwan sale follows the US$329 million sale last week of Tilcon Inc, BTR's quarrying and aggregate busines in the north-east of the United States. Page C3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
